suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the clause records Columbia Capital Management's unconditional acceptance of the engagement but imposes no express corresponding obligation on the City — most critically, no commitment to compensate Consultant for the services it has agreed to perform. While payment terms are likely addressed elsewhere in the Agreement, anchoring the City's reciprocal compensation obligation at the point of engagement provides Columbia Capital Management with a cleaner contractual basis should a payment dispute arise. Without it, the engagement clause reads as a one-way commitment by the Consultant only.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 1. Engagement. The City hereby engages Consultant as an independent contractor to perform the services described in this Agreement and Consultant accepts that engagement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 1. Engagement. The City hereby engages Consultant as an independent contractor to perform the services described in this Agreement, and the City shall compensate Consultant for such services in accordance with the terms of this Agreement, which Consultant hereby accepts.

suggestions.reason: The clause references Exhibit A for the description of Contract Services but contains no express exclusion of services outside that scope, leaving Columbia Capital Management exposed to City claims that additional or tangential work falls implicitly within the Contract Services and must be performed without further compensation. Without a clear exclusion provision, the vague "Investment Management Services" header in Exhibit A compounds this risk by giving the City a basis to argue that related advisory or administrative tasks are captured by the existing scope. The existing supplemental agreement mechanism protects Columbia Capital Management in theory, but only if the threshold question — whether a task is already within scope — is first resolved in Columbia Capital Management's favor, which the current language does not support. Adding an express exclusion anchored to Exhibit A closes this gap surgically.
suggestions.original_text: Scope of Services. Consultant shall perform those services (“Contract Services”) described under Scope of Services in Exhibit A, which is attached to this Agreement and incorporated herein by reference. The City may also request additional services not anticipated at the time of this Agreement. At the City’s request, the Consultant shall submit a written scope of the additional work including an estimate of additional costs for the performance of the additional work. No change in scope shall be effective nor additional compensation be paid, except on the basis of the provisions of a written supplemental agreement or an amendment signed by the Parties.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Scope of Services. Consultant shall perform those services ("Contract Services") described under Scope of Services in Exhibit A, which is attached to this Agreement and incorporated herein by reference. Any services not expressly described in Exhibit A are excluded from the Contract Services and shall not be construed as obligations of Consultant under this Agreement. The City may also request additional services not anticipated at the time of this Agreement. At the City's request, the Consultant shall submit a written scope of the additional work including an estimate of additional costs for the performance of the additional work. No change in scope shall be effective nor additional compensation be paid, except on the basis of the provisions of a written supplemental agreement or an amendment signed by the Parties.

suggestions.reason: Section 3 as drafted does nothing more than redirect to Exhibit A, leaving Columbia Capital Management entirely unprotected on the core mechanics of payment: there is no invoicing procedure, no payment deadline binding the City, no fixed-fee confirmation, no late-payment remedy, and no expense reimbursement framework. In practice, the City could delay payment indefinitely, contest invoices without constraint, and refuse expense reimbursement, and Columbia Capital Management would have no express contractual basis to enforce timely payment or accrue interest on overdue amounts. The absence of a dispute-and-pay mechanism is particularly damaging because it allows the City to withhold entire invoices on a minor objection rather than paying the undisputed balance while the dispute is resolved.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 3. Compensation and Expenses. As set forth in Exhibit A, the City shall pay the Consultant for the Contract Services it performs as outlined in Section 2 of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 3. Compensation and Expenses. As set forth in Exhibit A, the City shall pay the Consultant for the Contract Services it performs as outlined in Section 2 of this Agreement. The Consultant shall submit invoices to the City on a monthly basis, and the City shall remit payment of all undisputed amounts within thirty (30) days following receipt of each invoice. Fees are fixed as set forth in Exhibit A and shall not be modified except by written amendment executed by both parties. Reimbursable expenses, if any, shall be as specified in Exhibit A. If the City disputes any portion of an invoice, the City shall notify the Consultant in writing within fifteen (15) days of receipt, identifying the disputed amount and the basis for the dispute; undisputed amounts shall be paid by the original due date. Any invoice amount remaining unpaid after thirty (30) days shall accrue interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is less, until paid in full.

suggestions.reason: The clause permits the City to terminate for cause upon the same sixty (60) days' written notice applicable to convenience terminations, without affording Columbia Capital Management any opportunity to cure an alleged breach before termination takes effect — exposing the Consultant to immediate loss of a contract engagement over a potentially remediable issue. Without a defined cure period, the City retains unchecked leverage to terminate for cause even where Columbia Capital Management could have corrected the deficiency, creating material financial and reputational risk to the Consultant. Additionally, while a sixty (60) day notice period is stated for both parties, the clause does not expressly state that termination takes effect upon expiration of that notice period, leaving the effective date ambiguous and potentially litigable. The survival provision covers indemnity and insurance, which is consistent with Columbia Capital Management's continuing exposure under those sections post-termination.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 4. Termination of Agreement. The City may terminate this Agreement at any time on and after November 30, 2024, with sixty (60) days’ written notice for convenience or cause upon written notice to Consultant. If the City terminates the Agreement under this Section, the City shall pay the Consultant for Contract Services satisfactorily performed by Consultant before the termination, and for all associated expenses incurred by the Consultant before the termination. Under no circumstances will the Consultant be entitled to anticipatory profits or consequential damages. Consultant may terminate the agreement at any time upon sixty (60) days’ written notice. The provisions regarding indemnity and insurance shall survive the termination of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 4. Termination of Agreement. The City may terminate this Agreement at any time on and after November 30, 2024, with sixty (60) days' written notice for convenience, effective upon expiration of such notice period. For termination for cause, the City shall first provide Consultant with written notice specifying the alleged breach in reasonable detail, and Consultant shall have thirty (30) days following receipt of such notice to cure such breach; if the breach remains uncured at the expiration of such thirty (30) day cure period, termination shall take effect immediately thereafter. If the City terminates the Agreement under this Section, the City shall pay the Consultant for Contract Services satisfactorily performed by Consultant before the termination, and for all associated expenses incurred by the Consultant before the termination. Under no circumstances will the Consultant be entitled to anticipatory profits or consequential damages. Consultant may terminate the Agreement at any time upon sixty (60) days' written notice, effective upon expiration of such notice period. The provisions regarding indemnity and insurance shall survive the termination of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the compliance obligation in Section 6 imposes a broad, fault-neutral indemnification on Columbia Capital Management with no carve-out limiting liability to Consultant's own negligent or willful conduct, creating uncapped financial exposure for violations that may be technical, inadvertent, or caused by third parties. The clause also contains no mechanism to address the cost of mid-contract changes in law, meaning Columbia Capital Management would silently absorb any incremental compliance costs without any right to seek a fee adjustment from the City. Additionally, the clause omits market-standard references to anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and applicable labor standards, which creates regulatory ambiguity, and it does not require any notification upon a material legal violation affecting performance, leaving the City no basis to treat silence as a breach while also denying Columbia Capital Management any structured process to manage such events.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 6. Compliance with Laws. Consultant shall comply with local, state, and federal rules, regulations, and laws pertaining to this Agreement that are applicable at the time the Consultant conducts the Contract Services, regardless of whether such requirements are specifically referred to in this Agreement. Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents against any claim or liability arising from or based on any violation of the same.

suggestions.clause: Compliance with Equal Opportunity Laws, Regulations, and Rules
suggestions.reason: The clause covers anti-discrimination statutes but is silent on anti-bribery and corruption compliance, supply-chain labour standards (including forced labour and human trafficking), and any obligation to notify the City of a material legal breach affecting performance — gaps that, at the High risk level assessed here, expose Columbia Capital Management to disputed compliance expectations and potential mid-project termination claims if the City later asserts that uncodified standards were implicitly required. Without a defined compliance baseline, the City retains broad discretion to assert non-compliance under the general catch-all language found elsewhere in the Agreement, creating enforcement uncertainty that is commercially and reputationally adverse to Columbia Capital Management. The notification obligation is drafted as a mutual, material-breach trigger to avoid imposing a unilateral self-reporting burden on Columbia Capital Management.
suggestions.original_text: Discrimination Prohibited. Consultant agrees to comply with the Kansas Act Against Discrimination (K.S.A. 44-1001 et seq.) and the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act (K.S.A. 44-1111 et seq.) and shall not discriminate against any person in the performance of work under this Agreement because of race, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin or ancestry, or age.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Discrimination Prohibited. Consultant agrees to comply with the Kansas Act Against Discrimination (K.S.A. 44-1001 et seq.) and the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act (K.S.A. 44-1111 et seq.) and shall not discriminate against any person in the performance of work under this Agreement because of race, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin or ancestry, or age. Consultant further agrees to comply with applicable anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws and to maintain reasonable measures against forced labour and human trafficking in its performance of this Agreement. Each party shall promptly notify the other upon becoming aware of any material breach of applicable law that materially affects performance under this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The clause restricts the insurance maintenance obligation to "throughout the duration of this Agreement" without addressing post-termination claims-made exposure, leaving coverage continuity ambiguous for any policies that may operate on a claims-made basis by written agreement under the existing carve-out. More significantly for Columbia Capital Management, the clause is entirely silent on the relationship between the insurance requirements and the Consultant's underlying contractual liability: without an express non-expansion clause, the City could argue that the prescribed coverage amounts constitute a floor establishing the minimum scope of the Consultant's exposure, inadvertently broadening Columbia Capital Management's financial liability beyond any cap or limitation provided elsewhere in the Agreement. Adding a brief non-expansion sentence directly protects Columbia Capital Management from that construction while a narrow tail-coverage qualifier, limited to claims-made policies only, resolves the duration gap without imposing a blanket post-termination obligation on occurrence-based programs.
suggestions.original_text: General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The City shall be named as  an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers’ compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. All insurance procured for this Agreement by the Consultant, including additional insured designations, shall be primary and noncontributory. Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on forms acceptable to the City at the time of this Agreement’s execution. The Certificate shall specify the date when such insurance expires. A renewal certificate shall be furnished to the City before the expiration date of any coverage. The City shall be notified by receipt of written notice from the insurer at least 30 days before material modification or cancellation of any policy listed on the Certificate.
suggestions.suggested_fix: General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement, and for a period of one (1) year following expiration or termination of this Agreement solely with respect to any coverage maintained on a claims-made basis pursuant to written agreement, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The procurement and maintenance of insurance as required herein shall not be construed to expand, limit, or otherwise modify the Consultant's liability beyond the terms expressly set forth in this Agreement. The City shall be named as an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers' compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. All insurance procured for this Agreement by the Consultant, including additional insured designations, shall be primary and noncontributory. Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on forms acceptable to the City at the time of this Agreement's execution. The Certificate shall specify the date when such insurance expires. A renewal certificate shall be furnished to the City before the expiration date of any coverage. The City shall be notified by receipt of written notice from the insurer at least 30 days before material modification or cancellation of any policy listed on the Certificate.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 9 imposes a unilateral indemnification obligation exclusively on Columbia Capital Management (Consultant) with no reciprocal protection for acts or omissions of the City, exposing Consultant to open-ended liability for losses that may be caused substantially by the City's own conduct. The "Without in any way limiting" prefatory language is particularly dangerous because it expressly overrides any liability cap or limitation of liability provision that may exist elsewhere in the Agreement, rendering Consultant's financial exposure potentially uncapped. The notice obligation requiring "immediate" written notice of any claim imposes an unrealistically strict trigger that could be used by the City to defeat Consultant's indemnity rights if notification is delayed even briefly, and the clause contains no mechanism for Consultant to control the defense or approve settlements, nor does it require the City to take reasonable steps to mitigate its losses. These deficiencies together create material financial and operational risk for Columbia Capital Management that must be corrected.
suggestions.original_text: Section 9. Indemnification. Without in any way limiting indemnification obligations that may be set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the  City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys’ fees, arising out of or resulting from the performance of Consultant’s services, provided that any such claim, damage, loss, liability, cost, or expense is caused in whole or in part by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the Consultant, its subcontractors, anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them, or anyone for whose acts any of them may be liable, whether or not arising before or after completion of Consultant’s services. Consultant shall give the City immediate written notice of any claim, suit, or demand that may be subject to this provision.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 9. Indemnification. Subject to any limitation of liability provisions set forth in this Agreement, each party (the "Indemnifying Party") shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the other party and its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys' fees, arising out of or resulting from the Indemnifying Party's performance of its obligations under this Agreement, provided that any such claim, damage, loss, liability, cost, or expense is caused in whole or in part by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the Indemnifying Party, its subcontractors, or anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them. The indemnified party shall: (i) give the Indemnifying Party prompt written notice of any claim, suit, or demand subject to this provision; (ii) grant the Indemnifying Party reasonable control of the defense and settlement of such claim, provided that the Indemnifying Party shall not settle any claim that imposes liability or obligation on the indemnified party without the indemnified party's prior written consent; and (iii) take commercially reasonable steps to mitigate its losses.

suggestions.reason: The clause's prohibition on third-party suits is drafted narrowly, limiting its reach only to suits "for personal injuries or property damage," which creates an ambiguity that a court could resolve against Columbia Capital Management: a third party could plausibly argue that the enumeration of only those two categories implicitly leaves open third-party claims of other kinds — such as economic loss, breach of contract, or professional liability claims — arising from this Agreement. This interpretive gap exposes Columbia Capital Management to third-party suits that the parties plainly intended to foreclose, and two reasonable lawyers could read the current language to reach opposite conclusions on that point. The surgical fix is to replace the category-specific language with a general prohibition covering any suit or claim, eliminating the implied-authorization risk without altering the remaining structure of the clause.
suggestions.original_text: Section 10. No Third Party Beneficiaries. City and Consultant specifically agree that this Agreement is not intended to create any third party beneficiary relationship nor to authorize anyone not a party to this Agreement to maintain a suit for personal injuries or property damage pursuant to the terms or provisions of this Agreement; the duties, obligations and responsibilities of the parties to this Agreement with respect to third parties shall remain as imposed by law.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 10. No Third Party Beneficiaries. City and Consultant specifically agree that this Agreement is not intended to create any third party beneficiary relationship nor to authorize anyone not a party to this Agreement to maintain any suit or claim of any kind pursuant to the terms or provisions of this Agreement; the duties, obligations and responsibilities of the parties to this Agreement with respect to third parties shall remain as imposed by law.

suggestions.reason: As drafted, this clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to significant legal and financial risk on multiple fronts: the absence of a governing law and a designated forum leaves any dispute subject to contested jurisdictional arguments, while the vague "steps as it deems necessary" language creates no predictable or enforceable dispute resolution pathway. Most critically, the continue-performance obligation falls exclusively on the Consultant, meaning Columbia Capital Management must keep delivering services regardless of a dispute — including one arising from the City's own non-payment — with no reciprocal obligation on the City to continue paying. The negotiation step uses the precatory "should" rather than a binding obligation with a defined timeframe, undermining Columbia Capital Management's ability to enforce a structured pre-litigation process or demonstrate procedural compliance before a court.
suggestions.original_text: Section 11. Disputes. The City and Consultant agree that disputes relative to the Contract Services of this Agreement should first be addressed by negotiations between the parties. If direct negotiations fail to resolve the dispute, the party initiating the claim that is the basis of the dispute shall be free to take such steps as it deems necessary to protect its interest; provided, however, that notwithstanding any such dispute, the Consultant shall proceed with its services under this Agreement as though no dispute exists.

suggestions.reason: The existing representations clause for Columbia Capital Management (Consultant) is confined solely to a price-collusion representation, leaving the engagement's core performance standard, law-compliance obligations, and intellectual property exposure entirely undefined. Without a stated performance standard, the City retains the ability to invoke an implied standard that may exceed what the parties actually contemplated, creating open-ended liability for Columbia Capital Management. The absence of a defined remedy for any warranty breach is particularly damaging: without it, common-law remedies—including uncapped damages—remain available to the City, rather than being limited to the commercially appropriate remedy of re-performance, which would cap Columbia Capital Management's exposure. Establishing a bounded, market-standard warranty package now protects Columbia Capital Management by setting a defined ceiling on what the City can demand.
suggestions.original_text: The price submitted and the costs comprising same are independently arrived at without collusion.
suggestions.suggested_fix: The price submitted and the costs comprising same are independently arrived at without collusion. Consultant further warrants that the Services will be performed with professional skill and care consistent with applicable industry standards, that each party shall comply with applicable laws in performing its obligations under this Agreement, and that Consultant's independently created work product will not knowingly infringe the intellectual property rights of any third party; the City's sole and exclusive remedy for any breach of the foregoing warranties shall be re-performance of the non-conforming Services at no additional cost.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the authority representation runs exclusively against Columbia Capital Management, leaving the City with no corresponding obligation to warrant its own authority to enter and perform the Agreement; if the City in fact lacked requisite authorization, Columbia Capital Management would have no contractual basis to challenge the enforceability of the Agreement against the City. Additionally, the warranty contains no temporal anchor, meaning Columbia Capital Management's representation is of indefinite duration and could theoretically be invoked at any time following execution, creating open-ended exposure. Both deficiencies should be cured simultaneously: the representation must be made mutual, and it must be limited to the state of affairs as of the date the Agreement is executed.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant has all requisite power and authority to conduct its business and to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: As of the Effective Date, each party represents and warrants that it has all requisite power and authority to conduct its business and to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 13 imposes a dual warranty burden on Columbia Capital Management: first, that work shall "conform to or exceed" recognized professional standards, and second — an entirely separate and materially higher threshold — that work shall reflect "state of the art procedures and techniques in all relevant subject matters." The phrase "state of the art" is undefined in the Agreement and sets an aspirational, indeterminate standard well above the conventional industry-standard benchmark, exposing Columbia Capital Management to warranty claims measured against an unpredictable and potentially unachievable yardstick. Because the warranties are unqualified and uncapped on their face, a breach allegation under this elevated standard could translate into unlimited financial exposure for Columbia Capital Management, with no corresponding obligation on the City. The operative fix is to align the second warranty to the same objectively determinable professional standard as the first, eliminating the undefined "state of the art" language that creates asymmetric and open-ended liability risk.
suggestions.original_text: Section 13. Quality Assurance. Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement, shall conform to or exceed the recognized professional standards prevalent in their field. Further, the Consultant warrants that all work and service performed under this Agreement shall be performed with the professional expertise, skills, and knowledge of state of the art procedures and techniques in all relevant subject matters. The Consultant accordingly shall be capable of performing the necessary consulting and other services required herein and possess the ready comprehension of the required subject matter and the expertise to provide these services.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 13. Quality Assurance. Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement shall conform to recognized professional standards prevalent in their field. Further, the Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement shall be performed with the professional expertise, skills, and knowledge consistent with generally accepted professional standards and practices in the relevant field. The Consultant accordingly shall be capable of performing the necessary consulting and other services required herein and possess the ready comprehension of the required subject matter and the expertise to provide these services.

suggestions.reason: The current clause imposes a unilateral assignment restriction solely on Columbia Capital Management (Consultant), while imposing no corresponding restriction on the City and granting the City unfettered, standardless consent authority with no response obligation — exposing Columbia Capital Management to indefinite delay or arbitrary withholding of consent. The absence of any carve-out for affiliate transfers or corporate restructurings (merger, acquisition, or business sale) means that even an internal reorganization would technically require the City's approval, creating material operational risk for Columbia Capital Management. Additionally, the successor-and-assigns sentence purports to bind Consultant's successors "whether consented to or not," yet contains no express continuing-liability provision tethered to a written release, leaving ambiguity that could be used against Columbia Capital Management. The fix makes the restriction mutual, qualifies the City's consent right, and carves out permitted transfers for Columbia Capital Management's reorganizations and affiliates.
suggestions.original_text: Section 14. Assignment. Neither this Agreement nor any rights or obligations hereunder shall be assigned or otherwise transferred by Consultant without the prior written consent of the City. This Agreement is binding upon and fully enforceable against the successors and assigns of Consultant, whether consented to or not.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 14. Assignment. Neither this Agreement nor any rights or obligations hereunder shall be assigned or otherwise transferred by either party without the other party's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed; provided that Consultant may assign this Agreement, upon prior written notice to City, to an affiliate or in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all of its business without City's consent. Any permitted assignment shall not relieve the assigning party of its obligations hereunder unless expressly released in writing by the non-assigning party. This Agreement is binding upon the permitted successors and assigns of both parties.

suggestions.reason: The notice block for Columbia Capital Management contains only a static address with no mechanism for updating contact details, which creates a practical risk that notices sent to a superseded address could be deemed validly delivered against Columbia Capital Management even after a change of address or key contact. Without a change-of-notice procedure, City could rely on the hardcoded address indefinitely, potentially causing Columbia Capital Management to miss time-sensitive communications such as termination notices or cure demands. A brief update mechanism protects Columbia Capital Management's ability to redirect formal correspondence as its operational circumstances evolve.
suggestions.original_text: Columbia Capital Management, LLC Attn: Compliance Officer 6700 Antioch Rd., Suite 250 Merriam, KS 66204
suggestions.suggested_fix: Columbia Capital Management, LLC Attn: Compliance Officer 6700 Antioch Rd., Suite 250 Merriam, KS 66204. Either party may change its notice details by providing written notice of such change to the other party, effective ten (10) days following receipt of such notice.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 16 omits three standard independent contractor protections that are material to Columbia Capital Management's legal and financial position. First, the absence of any statement that Consultant controls the manner and means of performing the Services weakens the independent contractor characterization and exposes Columbia Capital Management to employment reclassification risk under federal and state law. Second, the tax and withholding obligation is stated exclusively against Consultant, without any corresponding acknowledgment that the City bears responsibility for its own personnel's costs, taxes, and benefits, creating an asymmetric burden on Columbia Capital Management. Third, the clause contains no mutual statement that neither party may bind the other, leaving Columbia Capital Management exposed to unauthorized commitment claims. The existing unilateral indemnification running solely from Consultant to the City in connection with tax liabilities compounds the asymmetry and should be replaced with a mutual personnel-responsibility formulation that does not impose a standalone indemnification burden on Columbia Capital Management.
suggestions.original_text: Section 16. Independent Contractor. In no event, while performing under this Agreement, shall Consultant be deemed to be acting as an employee of the City; rather, Consultant shall be deemed to be an independent contractor. Consultant shall be responsible for and pay all taxes and withholdings required by law upon the compensation paid under this Agreement, and shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City from liability in connection therewith. Nothing expressed herein or implied herein shall be construed as creating between Consultant and the City the relationships of employer and employee, principal and agent, a partnership, or a joint venture.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 16. Independent Contractor. In no event, while performing under this Agreement, shall Consultant be deemed to be acting as an employee of the City; rather, Consultant shall be deemed to be an independent contractor. Consultant shall control the manner and means by which the Services are performed under this Agreement. Each party shall be solely responsible for the compensation, taxes, withholdings, and benefits of its own respective personnel. Neither party shall have the authority to bind the other party to any obligation or commitment. Nothing expressed herein or implied herein shall be construed as creating between Consultant and the City the relationships of employer and employee, principal and agent, a partnership, or a joint venture.

suggestions.clause: Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law
suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 17 addresses only the City's payment obligations under the Kansas Cash-Basis Law but imposes no mutual compliance framework, no obligation on the City to notify Columbia Capital Management of a compliance breach affecting the Agreement, and no mechanism to adjust Consultant's compensation if a change in applicable law materially increases the cost of performance. The absence of a change-in-law cost-allocation provision is a direct financial exposure for Columbia Capital Management, as it could be forced to absorb unanticipated regulatory compliance costs without recourse. Additionally, the clause is entirely silent on anti-bribery and anti-corruption standards, which creates reputational and legal risk for the engagement if either party violates applicable law without triggering any contractual consequence or disclosure obligation.
suggestions.original_text: Section 17. Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law. This Agreement must comply with the applicable provisions of the Kansas Cash-Basis Law, K.S.A. 10-1101 et seq., as amended. The City is obligated only to pay periodic payments or monthly installments under this Agreement as may lawfully be made from funds budgeted and appropriated for the purposes set forth in this Agreement during the City’s current budget year. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, in the event that the City does not budget and appropriate funds for any renewal term, for any reason in its sole discretion, the parties agree that they shall be relieved of all obligations under this Agreement without penalty. To the extent that the City does budget and appropriate funds for the purposes set forth in this Agreement, the obligations of the parties shall remain as provided herein.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 17. Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law. This Agreement must comply with the applicable provisions of the Kansas Cash-Basis Law, K.S.A. 10-1101 et seq., as amended. Each party shall comply with all applicable laws and regulations, including applicable anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws, and shall promptly notify the other party in writing if it becomes aware of any breach of applicable law that materially affects this Agreement. If any change in applicable law materially increases the cost or burden of Consultant's performance, the parties shall negotiate in good faith an equitable adjustment to the fees payable under this Agreement. The City is obligated only to pay periodic payments or monthly installments under this Agreement as may lawfully be made from funds budgeted and appropriated for the purposes set forth in this Agreement during the City's current budget year. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, in the event that the City does not budget and appropriate funds for any renewal term, for any reason in its sole discretion, the parties agree that they shall be relieved of all obligations under this Agreement without penalty. To the extent that the City does budget and appropriate funds for the purposes set forth in this Agreement, the obligations of the parties shall remain as provided herein.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "legal actions arising out of this Agreement" creates a low but real interpretive risk for Columbia Capital Management: a court could read "legal actions" as excluding equitable proceedings (such as injunctions or specific performance) and "arising out of" as narrower than "relating to," potentially leaving certain disputes — including those with a close but indirect connection to the Agreement — outside the agreed venue. If the City were to initiate such proceedings in a different forum, Columbia Capital Management would face the burden and cost of contesting venue. Replacing the ambiguous phrase with standard "actions or proceedings, whether legal or equitable, arising out of or relating to" language eliminates that interpretive gap and locks in Johnson County District Court as the exclusive forum for all disputes between the parties.
suggestions.original_text: Section 18. Legal Action. The parties agree that the sole and exclusive venue for any legal actions arising out of this Agreement shall be the District Court of Johnson County, Kansas.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 18. Legal Action. The parties agree that the sole and exclusive venue for any actions or proceedings, whether legal or equitable, arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be the District Court of Johnson County, Kansas.

suggestions.reason: The current provision does no more than designate Kansas law, leaving five material structural gaps that expose Columbia Capital Management to significant litigation risk: there is no designated forum, meaning the City could file in any convenient or favorable court; there are no mandatory pre-litigation steps, eliminating a commercially valuable opportunity for Columbia Capital Management to resolve disputes before incurring legal costs; both parties are free to elect any forum, creating asymmetric risk; Columbia Capital Management has no express right to seek emergency injunctive or equitable relief without first triggering a lengthy dispute process; and nothing requires the City to continue performing its payment obligations—including remitting fees owed to Columbia Capital Management—while a dispute is pending. Because fees, scope, and deliverables are addressed elsewhere in the Agreement, the absence of a continued-performance obligation is a direct financial exposure for Columbia Capital Management.
suggestions.original_text: Section 19. Governing Law. This Agreement, the rights and obligations of the parties, and any claim or dispute arising hereunder shall be construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Kansas.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "automatically be considered reformed and amended so as to conform to all applicable legal requirements" is ambiguous in a manner that creates interpretive risk for Columbia Capital Management: it provides no standard or mechanism governing how the reformation is accomplished, leaving open whether the City, a court, or some other actor determines the reformed content, and to what extent. Because the reformation occurs "automatically" rather than through judicial or mutual intervention, a counterparty or court could interpret this language to maximize the scope of a reformulated obligation in a way unfavorable to Columbia Capital Management, rather than limiting reformation to the narrowest adjustment necessary to achieve validity. Anchoring the reformation standard to the minimum extent necessary to make the provision valid and enforceable removes that interpretive uncertainty and protects Columbia Capital Management from an expansive judicial or unilateral rewrite of any challenged provision.
suggestions.original_text: Section 22. Invalidity. If any provision in this Agreement shall be adjudicated invalid under applicable laws, such invalid provision shall automatically be considered reformed and amended so as to conform to all applicable legal requirements, or, if such invalidity cannot be cured by reformation or amendment, the same shall be considered stricken and deleted, but in neither such event or events shall the validity or enforceability of the remaining valid portions hereof be affected thereby.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 22. Invalidity. If any provision in this Agreement shall be adjudicated invalid under applicable laws, such invalid provision shall be reformed and amended by a court of competent jurisdiction to the minimum extent necessary to make such provision valid and enforceable under applicable law, or, if such invalidity cannot be cured by reformation or amendment, the same shall be considered stricken and deleted, but in neither such event or events shall the validity or enforceability of the remaining valid portions hereof be affected thereby.

suggestions.reason: The clause correctly provides that inaction does not constitute a waiver and that any waiver must be in writing, but it omits the standard protection that a waiver of one specific breach or right does not operate as a waiver of any other or future breach of the same or a different provision. Without this language, if Columbia Capital Management grants the City a one-time written accommodation on a contractual obligation, the City could argue that such waiver extends to other or subsequent breaches, potentially undermining Columbia Capital Management's ability to enforce the Agreement's terms going forward. This gap is particularly material in a professional services context where performance obligations and payment terms may be adjusted informally over time.
suggestions.original_text: Section 23. Waiver. The failure of either party to insist upon the strict performance of any of the terms or conditions of this Agreement or to exercise any option, right, or remedy herein contained, shall not be construed as a waiver or relinquishment for the future of such term, provision, option, right, or remedy, but the same shall continue and remain in full force and effect. No waiver by either party of any term or provision hereof shall be deemed to have been made unless expressed in writing and signed by the waiving party.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 23. Waiver. The failure of either party to insist upon the strict performance of any of the terms or conditions of this Agreement or to exercise any option, right, or remedy herein contained, shall not be construed as a waiver or relinquishment for the future of such term, provision, option, right, or remedy, but the same shall continue and remain in full force and effect. No waiver by either party of any term or provision hereof shall be deemed to have been made unless expressed in writing and signed by the waiving party. No waiver of any breach of any term or provision of this Agreement shall be construed as a waiver of any other or subsequent breach, whether of the same or a different term or provision.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "documents incorporated by reference" is undefined and unanchored: no schedule, exhibit list, or other provision in the clause identifies which documents are incorporated, meaning the City could argue that pre-contractual correspondence, proposal documents, or other materials form part of the Agreement, potentially expanding Columbia Capital Management's obligations beyond what was negotiated. Similarly, limiting the merger clause's scope to "professional services set forth herein" rather than the full subject matter of the Agreement creates an argument that matters not strictly labeled "professional services" fall outside the clause's integrating effect, undermining Columbia Capital Management's ability to defeat claims based on extrinsic representations or prior dealings. Both ambiguities expose Columbia Capital Management to disputes that a clearly drafted merger clause is designed to foreclose.
suggestions.original_text: Section 24. Merger. This Agreement and the documents incorporated by reference constitute the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the professional services set forth herein. There are no verbal understandings, agreements, representations or warranties between the parties that are not expressly set forth herein. This Agreement supersedes all prior agreements and understandings between the parties, both written and oral.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 24. Merger. This Agreement and any exhibits, schedules, or attachments expressly identified herein constitute the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof. There are no verbal understandings, agreements, representations or warranties between the parties that are not expressly set forth herein. This Agreement supersedes all prior agreements and understandings between the parties, both written and oral.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 25 only supersedes verbal statements made by City officials or representatives, leaving Columbia Capital Management exposed to claims that verbal statements made by its own personnel created binding commitments, modifications, or waivers of Agreement terms. This asymmetry means the City enjoys full protection against its own representatives' informal statements while Columbia Capital Management has no equivalent shield, a commercially unjustified imbalance with material operational risk on a professional services engagement where scope and deliverables are frequently discussed verbally. Making the integration clause mutual is a standard market-standard correction that counterparty counsel should readily accept.
suggestions.original_text: Section 25. Verbal Statements Not Binding. It is understood and agreed that the written terms and provisions of this Agreement supersede all verbal statements of any and every official or other representative of the City, and such statements shall not be effective or be construed as entering into, or forming a part of, or altering in any way whatsoever, this written Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 25. Verbal Statements Not Binding. It is understood and agreed that the written terms and provisions of this Agreement supersede all verbal statements of any and every official or other representative of either party, and such statements shall not be effective or be construed as entering into, or forming a part of, or altering in any way whatsoever, this written Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the Amendments clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to three compounding risks: the absence of an authorized-signatory requirement means the City could argue that communications or conduct by non-authorized personnel—or even by Columbia Capital Management's own project-level staff—constitute a binding amendment, potentially expanding Consultant's scope or reducing its fees without proper approval; the clause is silent on schedules and attachments, leaving the door open for the City to claim that informal changes to scope, pricing, or milestone schedules are effective without a signed written amendment; and without an express anti-oral-modification provision, the City could assert that course-of-dealing or oral direction altered Consultant's obligations under the Agreement. Each of these gaps creates meaningful financial and operational risk for Columbia Capital Management, particularly in a municipal engagement where scope creep and informal direction are common.
suggestions.original_text: Section 26. Amendments. This Agreement may not be amended unless such amendment is in writing and signed by both parties.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the survivorship clause imposes post-termination burdens exclusively on Columbia Capital Management—requiring indefinite maintenance of Insurance and Indemnification obligations—while imposing no corresponding post-termination obligations on City, most critically the obligation to pay any fees accrued and outstanding at termination. The open-ended catch-all, "any other terms and conditions that by their nature should survive termination," is sufficiently vague that City could invoke it to extend any provision of the Agreement against Columbia Capital Management after the engagement ends, creating indeterminate and potentially uncapped financial exposure. The absence of a durational limit on the surviving Indemnification obligation means Columbia Capital Management could face post-termination claims arising from stale allegations with no temporal ceiling. Removing the Insurance survival (which imposes an ongoing, unworkable maintenance burden post-engagement), capping Indemnification survival, adding City's payment survival obligation, and anchoring the catch-all to both parties equally and to express terms only resolves all four identified deficiencies.
suggestions.original_text: Section 27. Survivorship. Notwithstanding the termination of this Agreement, Consultant’s obligations with respect to Insurance (Section 8) and Indemnification (Section 9), and any other terms and conditions that by their nature should survive termination, shall survive the termination of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 27. Survivorship. Notwithstanding the termination of this Agreement, Consultant's obligations with respect to Indemnification (Section 9) shall survive the termination of this Agreement for a period of two (2) years following the effective date of such termination, and City's obligation to pay any fees or amounts accrued and unpaid as of the effective date of termination shall likewise survive termination. Any other terms and conditions that by their express written terms survive termination shall do so equally as to both parties.

suggestions.reason: The closing sentence imposes a sweeping, open-ended compliance covenant on Columbia Capital Management alone — requiring adherence to "all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking" — with no corresponding obligation on the City, creating a structurally one-sided appointment clause. The phrase "all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking" is materially ambiguous: two reasonable counsel could disagree on its scope, and a court could interpret it to encompass any statute, regulation, or ordinance arguably touching investment management, exposing Columbia Capital Management to unlimited compliance liability for legal requirements it may not have had reason to anticipate at execution. This uncapped, unqualified compliance obligation — untethered to a defined legal standard — could serve as a predicate for a breach claim arising from any regulatory development post-execution, without the City bearing any reciprocal duty to perform its own obligations under the Agreement. Replacing the vague phrase with the more precise and objective "applicable law" and adding a mutual performance obligation on the City restores commercial balance without altering the operative appointment mechanics.
suggestions.original_text: Appointment of Consultant. The City hereby appoints Consultant to act as the investment adviser and to assume the responsibilities of investment management of the pooled cash of the City including all idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts and bond proceeds (the “Accounts”). Consultant does hereby accept said appointment as an investment adviser under the Accounts. By accepting such appointment, Consultant agrees that at all times it shall act in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Appointment of Consultant. The City hereby appoints Consultant to act as the investment adviser and to assume the responsibilities of investment management of the pooled cash of the City including all idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts and bond proceeds (the "Accounts"). Consultant does hereby accept said appointment as an investment adviser under the Accounts. By accepting such appointment, Consultant agrees that at all times it shall act in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and applicable law. The City agrees that it shall likewise perform its obligations in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The "in addition to, but not in lieu of" construction expressly layers a contractual fiduciary standard on top of all applicable statutory standards, creating a separate and potentially broader basis for liability against Columbia Capital Management beyond what governing law already imposes — an additive exposure that is commercially unjustified and entirely one-sided. The undefined phrase "enterprise of like character and with like aims" introduces genuine interpretive ambiguity: without anchoring that benchmark to a public investment management context, the City could argue in a dispute that the applicable comparator enterprise carries a more demanding standard than the mandate Columbia Capital Management actually undertook. Additionally, the clause contains no limitation tethering the fiduciary duty to the scope of Columbia Capital Management's actual discretionary authority under the Agreement, which risks extending fiduciary exposure to decisions or outcomes outside the Consultant's control. Revising the clause to align the contractual standard with applicable law, anchoring the prudent-person benchmark to a public investment management mandate, and scoping the duty to the Consultant's discretionary authority eliminates these compounding risks.
suggestions.original_text: Fiduciary. In addition to, but not in lieu of any and all applicable fiduciary standards imposed under federal or state law, Consultant shall act as a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement. As a fiduciary, Consultant shall perform its duties under this Agreement with the care, skill, prudence, and diligence under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent person acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use in an enterprise of like character and with like aims.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Fiduciary. Consistent with applicable fiduciary standards imposed under federal or state law, Consultant shall act as a fiduciary solely with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement and solely within the scope of its discretionary authority thereunder. As a fiduciary, Consultant shall perform its duties under this Agreement with the care, skill, prudence, and diligence under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent investment manager acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use in managing a public investment portfolio of like character and with like aims.

suggestions.reason: The term "periodic" is undefined and affords no objective measure of how frequently Columbia Capital Management must deliver portfolio reports, exposing the Consultant to City claims that reporting was inadequate or untimely regardless of what was actually delivered. Equally, the word "including" renders the content list non-exhaustive, meaning the City could assert that additional data points—beyond holdings, transactions, portfolio income, and performance—were contractually required, creating an open-ended and unquantifiable service obligation against Columbia Capital Management. Without a defined frequency and a closed content list, a court could not resolve a reporting dispute from the face of the Agreement alone, leaving the Consultant vulnerable to adverse extrinsic interpretation.
suggestions.original_text: Providing periodic portfolio reporting to the City, including information on holdings, transactions, portfolio income and performance.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Providing quarterly portfolio reporting to the City, consisting of information on holdings, transactions, portfolio income, and performance.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted exposes Columbia Capital Management to two material risks. First, the City retains an unfettered right to change investment policy objectives and guidelines "from time to time" with no advance notice requirement or transition period, meaning Columbia Capital Management could be held in breach for executing trades under existing guidelines before it has any reasonable opportunity to implement newly issued guidelines. Second, the obligation to use investment strategies that "ensure" that "total explicit and implicit costs and total proceeds in every transaction are the most favorable under the circumstances" creates what amounts to an absolute warranty of best-priced execution on every trade — a standard that no professional investment manager can guarantee in volatile or illiquid markets and that would expose Columbia Capital Management to uncapped liability for any transaction in which a better price was theoretically available. These two provisions together — an uncontrolled unilateral power for the City to revise guidelines without notice, and an absolute transactional performance warranty — impose commercially unjustifiable obligations on Columbia Capital Management with no corresponding protection.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant shall invest and otherwise manage the assets held by the City, its banks and any Custodian in the Accounts. Responsibility for the investment and management is assigned to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have sole discretion with respect to investment of funds in the Accounts without prior consultation with the City; however, Consultant shall be bound by such written investment policy objectives and guidelines for the management of the assets as shall from time to time be provided to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have the authority to select the brokerage firms, consistent with the requirements of K.S.A. 12-1675(b)(4), through which orders will be placed. Consultant may combine orders for the Accounts with orders for other accounts or funds under management. Consultant shall effect all purchases and sales of securities in a manner consistent with the principles of best execution, taking into account net price (including commissions) and execution capability and other services that the broker or dealer may provide. Consultant shall use investment strategies designed to ensure that all securities transactions are executed in such a manner that the total explicit and implicit costs and total proceeds in every transaction are the most favorable under the circumstances. Consultant shall issue suitable instructions to the Custodian with respect to deliveries and payments.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Consultant shall invest and otherwise manage the assets held by the City, its banks and any Custodian in the Accounts. Responsibility for the investment and management is assigned to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have sole discretion with respect to investment of funds in the Accounts without prior consultation with the City; however, Consultant shall be bound by such written investment policy objectives and guidelines for the management of the assets as shall be provided to Consultant by the City in writing no fewer than thirty (30) days prior to the date on which such revised guidelines are to take effect. Consultant shall have the authority to select the brokerage firms, consistent with the requirements of K.S.A. 12-1675(b)(4), through which orders will be placed. Consultant may combine orders for the Accounts with orders for other accounts or funds under management. Consultant shall effect all purchases and sales of securities in a manner consistent with the principles of best execution, taking into account net price (including commissions) and execution capability and other services that the broker or dealer may provide. Consultant shall use commercially reasonable efforts and investment strategies designed to seek execution of securities transactions in a manner that targets favorable explicit and implicit costs and total proceeds under the prevailing market circumstances. Consultant shall issue suitable instructions to the Custodian with respect to deliveries and payments.

suggestions.reason: The word "Timely" imposes no objectively enforceable deadline on the City, meaning the City can delay providing account balances, statements, and interest-earned data indefinitely without being in breach, directly impairing Columbia Capital Management's ability to perform its advisory obligations under this Agreement. Because Columbia Capital Management's work product depends on current and accurate financial data from the City, an indeterminate delivery standard creates operational risk where the Consultant could be held accountable for performance failures caused by the City's own tardiness in supplying information. Additionally, the obligation lacks a clear trigger or condition — it is silent on whether delivery is prompted by a Consultant request, a recurring schedule, or a specific event — leaving Columbia Capital Management with no enforceable mechanism to compel timely production of the data it requires.
suggestions.original_text: Timely provide Consultant with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City’s funds and accounts.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Provide Consultant with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City's funds and accounts within five (5) Business Days following written request by Consultant.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "reasonable notice" is unanchored to any objective standard, leaving the City with broad discretion to characterize any notice from Columbia Capital Management as insufficient and thereby delay or refuse fund transfers — directly impeding Columbia Capital Management's ability to execute its investment plan on the City's behalf in a time-sensitive market environment. Similarly, "as necessary to effect the investment plan" is vague enough that the City could dispute whether a particular transfer qualifies as necessary, creating a basis to withhold cooperation and expose Columbia Capital Management to criticism for investment underperformance caused by the City's own inaction. Without a clear standard for both the adequacy of notice and the City's response obligation, Columbia Capital Management has no enforceable remedy if the City's delay causes missed investment opportunities or plan failures.
suggestions.original_text: Upon request and with reasonable notice, respond to Consultant’s requests to move money via Federal Reserve wire or other means between the City’s various accounts as necessary to effect the investment plan.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Upon request and with written notice reasonable under the circumstances of the required investment action, respond to Consultant's requests to move money via Federal Reserve wire or other means between the City's various accounts as necessary to effect the investment plan, and shall not unreasonably delay or withhold compliance with any such request.

suggestions.reason: The clause imposes no definite timeframe within which the City must instruct the Custodian to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased following receipt of Consultant's confirmations. For Columbia Capital Management, this creates material operational risk: if the City delays in issuing those instructions, securities settlements may fail, exposing Consultant to counterparty claims, failed-trade costs, or regulatory scrutiny arising from settlement defaults that are entirely outside Consultant's control. Anchoring the City's instruction obligation to a specific period following receipt of Consultant's confirmations directly protects Columbia Capital Management from settlement risk attributable to the City's inaction.
suggestions.original_text: Custodian. Pursuant to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1) the City shall instruct the Custodian to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased, including all expenses relating to the purchase and sale of such securities, such as brokerage commissions and transfer taxes, in accordance with copies of confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Custodian. Pursuant to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1) the City shall instruct the Custodian to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased, including all expenses relating to the purchase and sale of such securities, such as brokerage commissions and transfer taxes, within two (2) business days following receipt of copies of confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted contains no contractual obligation to disclose an actual or potential conflict of interest, leaving the City free to assert open-ended fiduciary or common-law claims against Columbia Capital Management if any undisclosed conflict later materializes, with no contractual benchmark defining what disclosure was required or when. That gap is commercially dangerous for Columbia Capital Management precisely because it has no safe harbor: compliance with an undefined duty is impossible to demonstrate after the fact. By adding a narrowly framed disclosure obligation—limited to known, material conflicts that directly affect the City's Accounts—Columbia Capital Management establishes a clear, objective compliance standard that cabins both its duty and the City's ability to allege concealment. The consequence language is drafted as a mutual good-faith determination, preserving Columbia Capital Management's operational flexibility rather than creating a unilateral City right to suspend or terminate.
suggestions.original_text: Potential Conflicts of Consultant. It is understood that Consultant will be acting in a similar capacity for other institutional clients, including other municipal governments in Kansas and that investments and reinvestments for the Accounts of the City may differ from those made or recommended with respect to the accounts and clients even though the investment objectives may be the same or similar; however, Consultant shall allocate investment opportunities among clients on a fair and equitable basis. In addition, Consultant serves as financial advisor to municipal governments within and beyond Kansas that issue bonds (an “Issuer Client”), including, in the case of Kansas issuers, bonds eligible for investment by the City. To prevent any appearances of favoring an issuer client over an investment client, or of favoring an investment client over an issuer client, it is the policy of Consultant to not purchase bonds of an Issuer Client issuing bonds in the primary market on behalf an investing client or to purchase callable bonds of an Issuer Client at any time on behalf of an investing client. This policy serves to protect both clients from potential conflicts but may limit investment opportunities for the City from time to time.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Potential Conflicts of Consultant. It is understood that Consultant will be acting in a similar capacity for other institutional clients, including other municipal governments in Kansas and that investments and reinvestments for the Accounts of the City may differ from those made or recommended with respect to the accounts and clients even though the investment objectives may be the same or similar; however, Consultant shall allocate investment opportunities among clients on a fair and equitable basis. Consultant shall promptly notify the City in writing of any known, material conflict of interest that directly affects the management of the City's Accounts, and upon such disclosure the parties shall in good faith determine an appropriate course of action with respect to the affected investment activity. In addition, Consultant serves as financial advisor to municipal governments within and beyond Kansas that issue bonds (an "Issuer Client"), including, in the case of Kansas issuers, bonds eligible for investment by the City. To prevent any appearances of favoring an issuer client over an investment client, or of favoring an investment client over an issuer client, it is the policy of Consultant to not purchase bonds of an Issuer Client issuing bonds in the primary market on behalf an investing client or to purchase callable bonds of an Issuer Client at any time on behalf of an investing client. This policy serves to protect both clients from potential conflicts but may limit investment opportunities for the City from time to time.

suggestions.reason: The City's unfettered right to amend Schedule X "at any time" with no specified advance notice period exposes Columbia Capital Management to material operational risk: the Consultant could act on instructions from an individual whose authority has been silently revoked or could be bound mid-engagement by unilateral authority changes without adequate time to adjust internal compliance and trading protocols. The phrase "with notice provided to Consultant" is fatally vague — it establishes no form, delivery method, or minimum period, meaning a court could not determine whether notice was validly given or when an amendment became binding on the Consultant. Additionally, the reference to "Schedule X" is an unfilled placeholder that must be completed prior to execution; until it is, the clause identifies no authorized City representative and the Consultant has no reliable basis on which to act. These combined deficiencies create significant legal uncertainty and operational exposure for Columbia Capital Management.
suggestions.original_text: Directions to Consultant. The names, titles and authorities of the individuals authorized to act on behalf of the City with respect to the Accounts and this Agreement are set forth in Schedule X to this Agreement, which is attached hereto and incorporated herein, and which may be amended in writing at any time by the City with notice provided to Consultant. Consultant may include information regarding the Accounts in aggregate performance data of Consultant that does not identify the City.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Directions to Consultant. The names, titles and authorities of the individuals authorized to act on behalf of the City with respect to the Accounts and this Agreement are set forth in Schedule X to this Agreement, which is attached hereto and incorporated herein, and which may be amended in writing by the City upon not less than five (5) Business Days' prior written notice to Consultant, with any such amendment becoming effective only upon Consultant's actual receipt of such written notice. Consultant may include information regarding the Accounts in aggregate performance data of Consultant that does not identify the City.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted leaves Columbia Capital Management materially exposed on several fronts: it does not specify when the City must pay an invoice, does not provide for interest or any other consequence if the City pays late, and contains no mechanism for Columbia Capital Management to adjust its fee schedule over the life of the engagement. Without a payment due date and a late-payment remedy, the City effectively holds an interest-free, open-ended payment obligation, undermining Columbia Capital Management's cash flow and leverage. The absence of an invoice dispute procedure also risks the City withholding entire invoices without obligation to pay the undisputed balance, further impairing Columbia Capital Management's revenue certainty.
suggestions.original_text: Management Fees. Consultant will be compensated for its services under this Agreement in an amount equal to 0.20% of the market value of the Accounts, billed quarterly in arrears based upon the average of the month-end Account balances for such quarter, with a minimum fee for each quarter of $3,000. Market value, including accrued income, will be determinative for the purpose of calculating fees. Such amount shall be the sole compensation owing by reason of investment advisory services under this Agreement. The fee for services for any period less than a full quarterly period will be pro-rated on a daily basis on the annualized fee for the period and on the market value of the portfolio as described on the final date of such period.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Management Fees. Consultant will be compensated for its services under this Agreement in an amount equal to 0.20% of the market value of the Accounts, billed quarterly in arrears based upon the average of the month-end Account balances for such quarter, with a minimum fee for each quarter of $3,000. Each invoice is due and payable within thirty (30) days following receipt. Any undisputed portion of an invoice shall remain due and payable by that date notwithstanding any good-faith dispute raised by City with respect to the remaining balance. Any amount not paid within thirty (30) days of the due date shall accrue interest at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law. Consultant's fee schedule may be adjusted upon not less than sixty (60) days' prior written notice to City. Market value, including accrued income, will be determinative for the purpose of calculating fees. Such amount shall be the sole compensation owing by reason of investment advisory services under this Agreement, excluding any pre-approved out-of-pocket expenses. The fee for services for any period less than a full quarterly period will be pro-rated on a daily basis on the annualized fee for the period and on the market value of the portfolio as described on the final date of such period.

suggestions.reason: As drafted, this clause imposes a unilateral disclosure obligation exclusively on Columbia Capital Management, requiring the Consultant to report events pertaining to the Accounts and/or itself, while placing no corresponding obligation on the City to notify the Consultant of events on its side that could equally affect the Accounts or the engagement. This asymmetry exposes Columbia Capital Management to a compliance burden and potential breach risk without any reciprocal information-sharing benefit from the City. In a managed-accounts relationship, the City's own financial decisions, funding changes, or administrative events are equally material to the Consultant's performance, and the absence of a reciprocal obligation leaves Columbia Capital Management commercially disadvantaged and operationally exposed.
suggestions.original_text: Notice of Events. Consultant shall provide written notice to the City regarding certain events pertaining to the Accounts and/or Consultant. Such notice shall include, at a minimum, the date, identification and description of the event triggering the notice requirement and shall be signed by an authorized party of Consultant.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Notice of Events. Consultant shall provide written notice to the City, and the City shall provide written notice to Consultant, regarding certain events pertaining to the Accounts and/or the notifying party. Such notice shall include, at a minimum, the date, identification and description of the event triggering the notice requirement and shall be signed by an authorized representative of the notifying party.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted contains a patent textual defect — "shall be immediately up the occurrence" — which is grammatically incomplete and operatively meaningless, exposing Columbia Capital Management to a dispute over whether a valid notice obligation exists at all and on what timeline it runs. Beyond the drafting error, the intended use of "immediately" imposes an open-ended, undefined standard that the City could weaponize against Columbia Capital Management by asserting that any notice delivered hours or days after a triggering event was untimely, creating a potential basis for claiming breach. Replacing the vague immediacy standard with a specific number of Business Days gives Columbia Capital Management a clear, objective deadline it can reliably meet, eliminating the City's ability to manufacture a notice default on ambiguous grounds.
suggestions.original_text: Written notice shall be immediately up the occurrence of any of the following events:
suggestions.suggested_fix: Written notice shall be provided within five (5) Business Days following the occurrence of any of the following events:

suggestions.reason: The term "significant" is undefined in this clause and, based on the review, nowhere in the Agreement, leaving its meaning entirely open to dispute. This ambiguity directly threatens Columbia Capital Management because the City could assert that virtually any legal action against the Consultant — regardless of how minor or unrelated to the engagement — qualifies as "significant," creating a broad and unpredictable disclosure obligation with potential breach consequences if the Consultant fails to report a matter the City later characterizes as significant. Anchoring the notice trigger to an objective, performance-based standard confines the obligation to legal actions that genuinely bear on Consultant's ability to deliver under this Agreement, eliminating the City's ability to invoke vague discretion to claim non-disclosure.
suggestions.original_text: Any significant legal actions instituted against Consultant or its members; and
suggestions.suggested_fix: Any legal actions instituted against Consultant or its members that would materially impair Consultant's ability to perform its obligations under this Agreement; and

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted limits Columbia Capital Management's representations solely to registration status under the Investment Consultants Act, leaving the Agreement silent on general legal compliance, intellectual property non-infringement, and any stated remedy for warranty breach. The absence of a legal compliance representation exposes the Agreement to challenge for incompleteness, while the lack of an IP non-infringement representation could invite the City to argue broader implied warranties under applicable law at Columbia Capital Management's expense. Critically, because no breach remedy is specified, Columbia Capital Management faces the risk that the City asserts open-ended or uncapped remedial rights; a defined, client-favorable remedy limits that exposure and governs in lieu of whatever general damages principles might otherwise apply.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant (i) is registered as an “investment adviser” under the Investment  Consultants Act of 1940 as amended (the “Consultants Act”); (ii) will promptly advise the City if at any time during the term of this Agreement Consultant ceases being so registered; and (iii) has delivered to the City a copy of Part II of its Form ADV or comparable Brochure pursuant to the Consultants Act;
suggestions.suggested_fix: Consultant (i) is registered as an "investment adviser" under the Investment Consultants Act of 1940 as amended (the "Consultants Act"); (ii) will promptly advise the City if at any time during the term of this Agreement Consultant ceases being so registered; (iii) has delivered to the City a copy of Part II of its Form ADV or comparable Brochure pursuant to the Consultants Act; (iv) is in material compliance with all applicable laws and regulations governing its performance of Services under this Agreement; and (v) to Consultant's knowledge, the Services do not infringe the intellectual property rights of any third party. In the event of a breach of any representation or warranty set forth in this Section, Consultant's sole obligation shall be to use commercially reasonable efforts to cure such breach promptly following written notice from City describing the alleged breach in reasonable detail.

suggestions.reason: The authority representation is currently unilateral, binding only Columbia Capital Management (as Consultant) while imposing no corresponding representation on the City of Westwood. If the City later claims it lacked proper authorization to enter this Agreement — for example, due to a failure to obtain requisite council approval or statutory authority — Columbia Capital Management would have no contractual basis to hold the City to its obligations or to recover fees and costs already incurred. A mutual authority representation is a standard, market-accepted protection that eliminates this enforceability gap at no commercial cost to Columbia Capital Management.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant is duly authorized and fully empowered to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Each party is duly authorized and fully empowered to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement.
